title: Dichotomy for the last-marker split
statement: For every Boolean word $v$, either $v$ contains no true bit and its last-true split is undefined, or there is a word $u$ such that $v$ contains a true bit, its last-true split is $u$, and for every Boolean word $p$, the last-true split of the concatenation $pv$ is $pu$.
replaced:
Every word $v$ satisfies exactly one of: $v$ contains no $1$ and the
last-marker split of $v$ is undefined; or $v$ contains a $1$ and the
last-marker split of $v$ is some word $u$ (the prefix of $v$ strictly before
its last $1$) such that moreover, for every prefix $p$, the last-marker split
of $p v$ is $p u$.
